Description The entire electrical system has been designed and constructed in accordance with the most up-to-date guidelines concerning safety and protection, especially against fire risks. There are two main kinds of protection: active protection, aimed at reducing possible causes of faults 'at source'; passive protection, aimed at minimizing the effects of a possible fault. The first kind involves the thoughtful design of wiring, attentive to location and anchorage, and the careful planning of properly protected cable routes. Modifications have therefore been made to the alternator and starter motor cables, with the adoption of protective caps. Passive protection instead includes all the interventions, which have always been adopted on vehicles, to reduce high fault currents (overload and short circuit). All the fuses included in the system have been rated on the basis of the nominal absorption of the loads which cannot be served simultaneously, and so as to ensure intervention in the case of a definite short circuit. All the electrical systems are supplied by the battery at a voltage of 12. V. The battery is, in turn, recharged by the alternator during engine operation. See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The main supply lines are protected by maxifuses, contained in two fuse boxes located near the battery and supplied directly from the latter. The power supplies for all the services and systems are protected by specific fuses, contained in the junction unit, or bridge fuses. The bridge fuses are located under the dashboard either just above the junction unit, or on the right above the glove compartment. All the power supplies are thus protected, except for the starter motor cable (battery-starter motor) and recharging cable (starter motor-alternator): these are protected by an additional shielded sheath. Some circuits are supplied continuously, even if the vehicle is stopped and the ignition is off, as they are connected directly to the battery. Other circuits are supplied by turning the ignition key to various different positions: when the key is inserted and turned to the first click, the ignition is turned on (MAR position) and several circuits are supplied, which are thus called 'ignition-operated' (lines 'INTE' and '15/54'); the second click - start up position - supplies the starter motor; (line '50')., disconnecting some circuits (those which absorb most power), thus ensuring the maximum flow of current to the starter motor; ('INT/A' line). on the other hand, by extracting the key and turning it in the opposite direction (and pressing the special button) the PARK position is engaged which supplies the side lights even with the key switched off ('STAZ' and 'POS' lines); See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS The lines through which the supply is distributed to the various electrical devices are shown on the wiring diagrams relating to the various functions and systems. This general diagram shows all the lines which depart from the battery, the maxifuse boxes and the ignition switch; reference should be made to the specific diagrams for greater detail.

Functional description All the electrical equipment and systems are supplied by the battery A1 . Description The entire electrical system has been designed and constructed in accordance with the most up-to-date guidelines concerning safety and protection, especially against fire risks. There are two main kinds of protection: active protection, aimed at reducing possible causes of faults 'at source'; passive protection, aimed at minimizing the effects of a possible fault. The first category involves careful design of wiring with thorough positioning and anchorage. Wiring is shielded and protected and the routes are carefully determined. Modifications have therefore been made to the alternator and starter motor cables, with the adoption of protective caps, etc. Passive protection instead includes all the interventions, which have always been adopted on vehicles, to reduce high fault currents (overload and short circuit). All the fuses included in the system have been rated on the basis of the nominal absorption of the loads which cannot be served simultaneously, and so as to ensure intervention in the case of a definite short circuit. All the electrical systems are supplied by the battery at a voltage of 12. V. The battery is in turn recharged by the alternator ( ) during engine operation. See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The main supply lines are protected by maxifuses, contained in two fuse boxes located near the battery and supplied directly from the latter. The power supplies for all the services and systems are protected by specific fuses, contained in the junction unit, or shunt fuses. The shunt fuses are located under the dashboard either just above the junction unit, or on the right above the glove compartment. All the power supplies are thus protected, except for the starter motor cable (battery-starter motor) and recharging cable (starter motor-alternator): these are protected by an additional shielded sheath. Some circuits are supplied continuously, even if the vehicle is stopped and the ignition is off, as they are connected directly to the battery. Other circuits are supplied by turning the ignition key to various different positions: when the key is inserted and turned to the first click, the ignition is turned on (MAR position) and several circuits are supplied, which are thus called 'ignition-operated' (lines 'INT' and '15/54'); the second click - AVV position - instead supplies the starter motor; (line '50')., disconnecting some circuits (those which absorb most power), thus ensuring the maximum flow of current to the starter motor; ('INT/A' line) on the other hand, by extracting the key and turning it in the opposite direction (and pressing the special button) the PARK position is engaged which supplies the side lights even with the key switched off ('STAZ' and 'POS' lines); (see E2010 - SIDE LIGHTS / NO. Description The entire electrical system has been designed and constructed in accordance with the most up-to-date guidelines concerning safety and protection, especially against fire risks. There are two main kinds of protection: active protection, aimed at reducing possible causes of faults 'at source'; passive protection, aimed at minimizing the effects of a possible fault. The first category involves careful design of wiring with thorough positioning and anchorage. Wiring is shielded and protected and the routes are carefully determined. Modifications have therefore been made to the alternator and starter motor cables, with the adoption of protective caps, etc. Passive protection instead includes all the interventions, which have always been adopted on vehicles, to reduce high fault currents (overload and short circuit). All the fuses included in the system have been rated on the basis of the nominal absorption of the loads which cannot be served simultaneously, and so as to ensure intervention in the case of a definite short circuit. All the electrical systems are supplied by the battery at a voltage of 12. V. The battery is in turn recharged by the alternator ( ) during engine operation. See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The main supply lines are protected by maxifuses, contained in two fuse boxes located near the battery and supplied directly from the latter. The power supplies for all the services and systems are protected by specific fuses, contained in the junction unit, or shunt fuses. The shunt fuses are located under the dashboard either just above the junction unit, or on the right above the glove compartment. All the power supplies are thus protected, except for the starter motor cable (battery-starter motor) and recharging cable (starter motor-alternator): these are protected by an additional shielded sheath. Some circuits are supplied continuously, even if the vehicle is stopped and the ignition is off, as they are connected directly to the battery. See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. Description The entire electrical system has been designed and constructed in accordance with the most up-to-date guidelines concerning safety and protection, especially against fire risks. There are two main kinds of protection: active protection, aimed at reducing possible causes of faults 'at source'; passive protection, aimed at minimizing the effects of a possible fault. The first category involves careful design of wiring with thorough positioning and anchorage. Wiring is shielded and protected and the routes are carefully determined. Modifications have therefore been made to the alternator and starter motor cables, with the adoption of protective caps, etc. Passive protection instead includes all the interventions, which have always been adopted on vehicles, to reduce high fault currents (overload and short circuit). All the fuses included in the system have been rated on the basis of the nominal absorption of the loads which cannot be served simultaneously, and so as to ensure intervention in the case of a definite short circuit. All the electrical systems are supplied by the battery at a voltage of 12. V. The battery is in turn recharged by the alternator ( ) during engine operation. See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The main supply lines are protected by maxifuses, contained in two fuse boxes located near the battery and supplied directly from the latter. The power supplies for all the services and systems are protected by specific fuses, contained in the junction unit, or shunt fuses. The shunt fuses are located under the dashboard either just above the junction unit, or on the right above the glove compartment. All the power supplies are thus protected, except for the starter motor cable (battery-starter motor) and recharging cable (starter motor-alternator): these are protected by an additional shielded sheath. Some circuits are supplied continuously, even if the vehicle is stopped and the ignition is off, as they are connected directly to the battery. Other circuits are supplied by turning the ignition key to various different positions: when the key is inserted and turned to the first click, the ignition is turned on (MAR position) and several circuits are supplied, which are thus called 'ignition-operated' (lines 'INT' and '15/54'); the second click - start up position - supplies the starter motor; (line '50')., disconnecting some circuits (those which absorb most power), thus ensuring the maximum flow of current to the starter motor; ('INT/A' line). on the other hand, by extracting the key and turning it in the opposite direction (and pressing the special button) the PARK position is engaged which supplies the side lights even with the key switched off ('STAZ' and 'POS' lines); ( ). See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. Description The following diagram shows the various earths on the vehicle, and the circuits connected to each are indicated. It is thus easy to identify the circuits which are connected to earth from the same line; this facilitates fault finding if a problem involves more than one function: for example, the corrosion of one earth could put different circuits and several functions out of action at the same time. Several earths belonging to the same wiring are connected to one another, through the various joins in the actual wiring. This makes it possible to correctly connect all the electrical components on the same wiring to earth, even if one particular earth point does not guarantee an efficient contact to the vehicle bodyshell.

Description The side lights are switched on when the ring nut on the steering column is turned to the first position, with the ignition in the ON position. They can also be turned on by extracting the key and turning it in the opposite direction - PARK position - keeping the special button pressed. Turning on the side lights also turns on the number plate lights and numerous other interior lights for passenger compartment lighting and instrument & control lighting (these lines are described and illustrated in the diagrams for the components to which they refer). The circuit for the side lights is protected by two fuses, in the junction unit; one for the right front and left rear side lights, the other for the left front and right rear side lights. A warning light in the instrument panel indicates that the side lights have been switched on.

Functional description The signal for activating the side lights reaches the ignition switch H1 (STAZ) when the steering column switch unit H5 - connector B pin 6 - is in the appropriate position: it is a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) for the line protected by fuse F8 of the junction unit B1 . Alternatively - with the key in the PARK position - the supply arrives directly from the battery (IGN maxifuse for B5 ). From switch H1 (POS) the supply is sent to the various side lights through the lines protected by fuses F2 and F3 for the junction unit B1 . The former protects the circuits for the right front F11 , left rear F30 and right number plate F51 lights. The second protects the circuits for the left front F10 , right rear F31 and left number plate F50 lights. At the same time, the side lights on warning light is supplied inside the instrument E50 - pin 1 for connector B -, whilst pin 3 for connector A of E50 acts as an earth. Description The vehicle has two special lamps for the dipped beam headlamps. The dipped beam headlamps are switched on through the steering column switch unit by turning the special ring nut in the position after the side lights. A special relay - under the dashboard next to the junction unit - keeps the dipped beam headlamps on with the main beam headlamps on. The circuit is protected by two fuses, one for the right hand headlamp, one for the left hand headlamp. The dipped beam headlamps circuit also gives the go ahead for the operation of the headlamp alignment and the headlamp washer circuit.

Functional description The circuit for the dipped beam headlamps is operated by the steering column switch unit H5 . By placing the switch in the dipped beam position, the line which supplies the headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right) is supplied controlled by the ignition. Each circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit B1 : F5 for the right headlamp and F4 for the left one. With the dipped beam headlamps on, this supply passes through the dipped beam headlamps maintenance relay/remote control switch J45 . If the dipped beam and main beam headlamps are switched, this supply is interrupted, but it is replaced by the one supplied from pin 87 of remote control switch J45 : the signal for switchign on the main beam headlamps - through the line for fuse F7 of the junction unit B1 - energizes the relay (pin 85) which switches the supply at the direct line (maxifuse J/B2 for B5 ) which keeps the circuit for the dipped headlamps and the main beam headlamps supplied. The supply line for the right lamp - protected by fuse F5 - also acts as the go ahead signal for the headlamp alignment ( ) and the headlamp washer ( See E3080 HEADLAMP AGLINMENT CORRECTOR ). See E3022 HEADLAMP WASHER

Description The vehicle has two special lamps for the main beam headlamps. These are switched on: with the dipped beam headlamps switched on by pushing the steering column switch unit lever towards the dashboard (stable mode) in 'flash' mode, by pulling the lever towards the steering wheel (unstable mode) The circuit is protected by two fuses in the junction unit, one for the right lamp and one for the left lamp. A warning light in the instrument panel signals that the main beam headlamps have been switched on.

Functional description The main beam headlamps circuit is operated by the steering column switch unit H5 . By placing the switch in the main beam position or by closing the 'flashing' contacts, the (left) F12 and (right) F13 lights are supplied: it involves a supply controlled by the ignition (INT/A) for the line protected by fuses F6 and F7 of the junction unit B1 , for the left and right headlamps, respectively. The supply line for the right headlamp also sends a signal to the instrument E50 - pin 12 for connector C - in order to supply the 'main beam headlamps on' warning light; pin 1 for connector B of E50 acts as an earth.

Description The vehicle is equipped with two main in the headlamps. These are activated: with the dipped beams on, by pushing the stalk toward the facia (stable mode) in flashing mode, by pulling the lever toward the steering wheel (unstable mode) The circuit is protected by two fuses located in the junction unit, one for the right headlight and one for the left headlight. Operational description The circuit for the main beam headlights is activated by the steering column switch unit H5 . Placing the switch in the main beam headlights position or closing the "flashing" contact supplies the main beams for the headlights F10 (left) and F11 (right): the supply is ignition operated (INT/A) for the line protected by fuses F6 and F7 from the junction unit B1 for the right and left headlights, respectively. Description The direction indicators and hazard warning lights delimit the outer dimensions of the car. The left and right direction indicators are operated by raising or lowering the appropriate lever on the stalk unit. The hazard warning lights (right and left direction indicators operated simultaneously) are turned on by the pressing the red button at the centre of the dashboard. The turn signals are activated with the ignition key on; For safety reasons, the hazard warning lights can be turned on at any time, as they are supplied directly from the battery. The circuits for the direction indicators and hazard warning lights are protected by two different fuses. Two warning lights on the dashboard, also flashing, indicate when the left and right direction indicators are turned on; one only if there is a trailer., The red hazard warning light button contains two leds: the first green one is ignition-operated and lights up the specific symbol; The second red light comes on intermittently when the hazard warning lights are operated. Versions with alarm: the hazard warning lights are also operated by the alarm system, which is connected directly to the lights power supply. Versions without alarm: the hazard warning lights are operated - when the door remote control is activated - by a special relay next to the junction unit. The hazard warning lights are also operated by the alarm system, which is connected directly to the power supply to the lights. Connection for towing a trailer: by replacing the intermittent device with a double device, the connection which signals that the right or left direction indicator has been switched on through a special warning light in the dashboard is activated.

Functional description The circuit is controlled by the switch control unit H90 . The intermittent device is located on the steering column switch unit H5. It is connected to earth to pin 7 of connector A and receives a supply signal to pin 7 of connector D through switch H90 itself, when: the hazard lights are not on, the supply is controlled by the ignition (INT) through the line for fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 . the hazard lights are on, the supply is direct from the battery through the line for maxifuse J/B1 of B5 and fuse F9 of junction unit B1 . The intermittent device therefore produces a signal which supplies both the switch for the direction indicators on the steering column switch unit H5 and the switch for the hazard warning lights H90 . The operation, in one direction or another, of the steering column switch lever H5 supplies the right direction indicators ( F11 , F21 , F31 ) or the left ones ( F10 , F20 , F30 ). At the same time, the warning light, located in the instrument panel E50 , comes on. By pressing the switch in the control panel H90 three contacts which simultaneously supply all the lights (right branch and left branch) close and the red LED in the actual switch which lights up the ideogram. There is also a special LED in the switch H90 which comes on when the ignition is switched on (INT/A) and is protected by fuse B27 . Versions with alarm: all the hazard warning lights are also operated by the alarm system control unit M30 (pins 1 and 2 of connector B), which is connected directly to the light power supply ( ). See E7015 ALARM Versions without alarm: all the hazard warning light are activated by the relay J43 which receives a direct supply from the battery, via the line for maxifuse J/B1 of B5 and fuse F9 of the junction unit B1 : the relay is energized by a signal coming from the receiver for the remote control M35 , pin 1. All the hazard warning lights are also operated by the alarm system control unit M30 (pins 1 and 2 of connector B), which is connected directly to the light power supply ( ). See E7015 ALARM Connection for towing a trailer: by replacing the intermittent device with a double device, this also produces an output signal - pin R - which supplies the warning light in the on board instrument E50 - pin 16 of connector C - which signals that the trailer direction indicators have been switched on.

Versions without alarm: the hazard warning lights are operated - when the door remote control is activated - by a special relay next to the junction unit. The hazard warning lights are also operated by the alarm system, which is connected directly to the power supply to the lights. Connection for towing a trailer: by replacing the intermittent device with a double device, the connection which signals that the right or left direction indicator has been switched on through a special warning light in the dashboard is activated.

Functional description The circuit is controlled by the switch control unit H90 . The intermittent device is located on the steering column switch unit H5. It is connected to earth to pin 7 of connector A and receives a supply signal to pin 7 of connector D through switch H90 itself, when: the hazard lights are not on: the supply is controlled by the ignition (INT) through fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 . the hazard lights are on: the supply is direct from the battery through the line of maxifuse J/B1 of B5 and fuse F9 of junction unit B1. The intermittent device therefore produces a signal which supplies both the switch for the direction indicators on the steering column switch unit H5 and the switch for the hazard warning lights H90 . The operation, in one direction or another, of the steering column switch lever H5 supplies the right direction indicators ( F11 , F21 , F31 ) or the left ones ( F10 , F20 , F30 ). At the same time, the warning light, located in the instrument panel E50 , comes on. By pressing the switch in the control panel H90 three contacts which simultaneously supply all the lights (right branch and left branch) close and the red LED in the actual switch which lights up the ideogram. There is also a special LED in the switch H90 which comes on when the ignition is switched on (INT/A) and is protected by fuse B27 . Versions with alarm: all the hazard warning lights are also operated by the alarm system control unit M30 (pins 1 and 2 of connector B), which is connected directly to the light power supply ( ). See E7015 ALARM Versions without alarm: all the hazard warning lights are operated by the relay J43 which receives a direct supply from the battery, via the line for the maxifuse J/B1 of B5 and fuse F9 of the junction unit B1 : the relay is energized by a signal coming from the receiver for the remote control M35 , pin 1.

Description The intermittent turn signals and hazard warning lights delimit the entire vehicle perimeter. The right and left side turn signals are activated by raising or lowering a steering wheel stalk switch. The hazard warning lights (right and left side indicators operated simultaneously) are activated by means of a red button in the centre of the control panel in the dashboard. The turn signals are ignition-operated but the hazard warning lights can always be operated for safety reasons because they are supplied directly by the battery. The turn signal and hazard warning light circuits are protected by two different fuses. Two warning lights in the instrument panel, also the intermittent type, signal that the left and right indicators have been switched on; one is only for if there is a trailer fitted. There are two LEDs in the red hazard warning lights button: the first is ignition-operated and lights up the ideogram; the second, red one, comes on intermittently when the hazard warning lights are activated. Versions with alarm: the hazard warning lights are also activated by the alarm system which is connected directly to the power supply for these lights. Versions without alarm: the hazard warning lights are operated - when the door remote control is activated - by a special relay next to the junction unit. The hazard warning lights are also activated by the alarm system which is connected directly to the power supply for these lights. Connection for a trailer: by replacing the intermittent device with a double charge it is possible to activate the connection that signals that either the left or the right indicator has been switched on by means of a special warning light in the instrument panel.

Operational description The circuit is controlled by the switch control unit H90 . The intermittent type device is located in the steering column switch unit H5. It is earthed at pin 7 of connector A and receives a supply signal at pin 7 of connector D via the actual switch H90, when: the hazard warning lights are not on: the power supply is ignition-operated (INT) via fuse F1 of junction unit B1 the hazard warning lights are on: the power supply comes directly from the battery via the line for maxifuse J/B1 of B5 and fuse F9 of junction unit B1 . The intermittent device then produces a signal which supplies both the switch for the steering column switch unit direction indicators H5 and the switch for the hazard warning lights H90 . Operating the lever for the steering column switch unit H5 in either direction provides a power supply for the right indicators ( F11 , F21 , F31 ) or the left ones ( F10 , F20 , F30 ). The warning light, located in the instrument panel E50 comes on simultaneously . By pressing the switch in the control unit H90 on the other hand the three contacts that simultaneously supply all the lights (left and right branches) and the red LED in the actual switch that lights up the ideogram are closed. In switch H90 there is also a special LED that comes on through the ignition-operated supply (INT/A) protected by shunt fuse B27 . Versions with alarm: all the hazard warning lights are also activated by the alarm system control unit M30 ). Vedere E7015 ALLARME ) Versions without alarm: all the hazard warning lights are activated by relay J43 which receives a direct supply from the battery, via the line for maxifuse J/B1 of B5 and fuse F9 of junction unit B1 : the relay is energized by a signal coming from the remote control receiver M35 , pin 1.

Description The brake lights are located at the rear in the side lights and in the central third brake light and consist of 10 separate bulbs. All three bulbs are operated whenever the brake pedal is pressed, by means of a switch on the pedal itself. The circuit is supplied with the ignition switched ON and is protected by a fuse, in the junction unit. A braking signal is also sent from the switch to the ABS, which detects braking status and therefore introduces braking control. The same signal is also sent to the JTD engine management system, which takes the braking condition into account when determining the engine control mode. On versions equipped with radios, a switch is fitted on the brake pedal with a special filter to prevent interference when the pedal is pressed.

Functional description The switch I30 is supplied when the ignition is switched on (INT) from the line protected by the fuse F1 for the junction unit B1 . When the brake pedal is pressed, the switch closes and sends the supply to the side brake lights in the rear light clusters F30 and F31 and to the centre rear light F40 .

Description The vehicle has two additional fog lamps for use in poor visibility conditions. The fog lamps are activated through a special button in the switch panel in the centre of the dashboard; this button, which is slightly lit with the ignition switched ON, becomes much brighter when the actual lights are switched on. The circuit for the fog lamps is protected by a special fuse and operated by a special relay, next to the junction unit. The fog lamps only come on when the side lights are switched on. In addition, if the key is turned ot the OFF position or the side lights are switched off, the fog lamps are switched off even if the button is pressed: this control logic is managed by a special electronic device located inside the switch unit.

Functional description The fog lights circuit is controlled by a special relay J40 ; the relay coil is supplied with the side lights switched on by the supply line controlled by the ignition protected by fuse F8 for the junction unit B1 ( ). See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS This line also sends a signal to the switch unit H90 (pin 2 for connector A) giving the go ahead to switch on the actual fog lamps. The energizing of the coil takes place through the closure of the special fog lamps switch in the switch unit H90 (pin 12 for connector A). This signal also lights up the actual button. The power line for the fog lamps relay is supplied directly by the battery via the maxifuse J/B2 of B5 and is protected by the special fuse B13 . Once energized, the relay supplies the two fog lamps F15 (left) and F16 (right). Description The vehicle is equipped with two extra-penetration fog lamps in the headlights for use in the case of poor visibility. The fog lights are activated using the special button in the switch unitt located in the centre of the dashboard; the button, dimly lit when the ignition is ON, then lights up more brightly when the actual lights are activated. The fog lights circuit is protected by a special shunt fuse and controlled by a specific relay, located next to the junction unit. The side lights must be switched on in order to switch the fog lights on. If the ignition key is switched OFF or the side lights are turned off, the fog lights are deactivated even if the operating button is still pressed: this control logic is managed by a special electronic device located inside the switch unit

Operational description The fog lights circuit is controlled by a special relay J40 ; the relay coil is supplied with the side lights on by the ignition-operated supply line protected by fuse F8 of junction unit B1 ( Vedere E2010 LUCI POSIZIONE / TARGA ). This line also sends a signal to switch unit H90 (pin 2 of connector A) for the go ahead to switch on the actual fog lights. The coil is energized by means of the closing of the special "fog lights on" switch located in the switch unit H90 (pin 12 of connector A). This signal also lights up the actual button. The power line for the fog lights relay receives a direct supply from the battery via maxifuse J/B2 of B5 and is protected by the special fuse B13 . Once energized, the relay supplies the fog lights for the (left) headlights F10 and the (right) headlights F11. The entire control unit H90 is lit up with the ignition on (INT/A) by the line (pin 5 of connector A) protected by shunt fuse B27 .

Description The front interior light includes two courtesy lights with two control switches. With the left switch (A) it is possible to select the following two operating modes: centre position: both lights on dependent on the opening of the doors; left-hand position: both lights are off all the time; right-hand position: both lights are on all the time. With the right switch (B) is it only possible to switch on one of the lights (map reading light): left-hand position: left-hand light always on; right-hand position: right-hand light always on; central position: both lights always off. Both rear interior lights contain a courtesy light that operates in different modes according to the position of the lens, which operates an internal switch. neutral position: light on dependent on the opening of the doors; positioned to one side: lights always off; positioned to the other side: light always on. The courtesy light timing is controlled according to a logic managed by the integrated services control unit, under the dashboard, which can be summarized as follows: when any of the doors are opened, all front and rear courtesy lights come on in timed mode: timed period of 6 seconds when the locks are unlocked using the key or the remote control; timed period of 6 seconds when a previously-opened door is reclosed; timing is suspended when the key is turned to MAR (this function allows the driver to enter the car and insert the key in the ignition) timed interval of 3 minutes if one of the doors is left open (this function prevents the battery going flat if the car is left with a door open) When one of the other doors is opened, the current timer count is reset to zero. The operation of the courtesy lights takes place coming on and going off gradually (dimmer function) and lasts about 3 seconds. The courtesy light circuit is protected by a special junction unit fuse.

Functional description The supply for the front courtesy lights ( G10 ) and the rear courtesy lights ( G25 and G26 ) arrives directly from the battery (maxifuse J/B1 for B5 ) through fuse F10 of the junction unit B1 . They are switched on via a direct earth signal (permanently activated) at pin 1 for the courtesy lights or at pin 3 by a signal from the integrated services control unit M40 . The control unit M40 is supplied directly from the battery at pin 8 of connector B through the line of the maxifuse J/B2 of B5 via fuse F19 and via the ignition (INT) - pin 7 of connector B - from line of fuse F1 from the junction unit B1 . Pin 13 of connector B provides the earth. The control unit receives door release and lock signals, which arrive: at pins 2 and 3 of connector B: opening of one of the front doors N50 and N51 (left and right respectively); at pins 12 and 18 of connector B: opening of one of the rear doors N55 and N56 (left and right, respectively). On the basis of the above signals and the control sequence described above, control unit M40 sends timed earth signals from pins 10 and 1 of connector C, which control front courtesy lights G10 and rear courtesy lights G25 and G26 .

Description The front courtesy light includes two courtesy lights with two control switches. The left switch (A) can be used to select the following operating modes: centre position: both lights switched on with a delay dependent on the opening of the doors; left position: both lights permanently off; right position: both lights permanently on. The two rear ceiling lights contain a courtesy light with different operating modes depending on the position of the actual lens cover which activates an internal switch: neutral position: light on with a delay dependent on the opening of the doors; position to one side: light always off; position to the other side: light permanently on. The courtesy lights are switched on and off gradually (dimmer function) over a period lasting around 3 seconds. The courtesy lights circuit is protected by a special fuse in the junction unit.

Pin 13 of connector B provides the earth. The junction unit receives the unlocking and opening signals for the doors which arrive: at pins 2 and 3 of connector B: opening of one of the front doors N50 and N51 (left and right, respectively); at pins 12 and 18 of connector B: opening of one of the rear doors N55 and N56 (left and right, respectively). On the basis of the above signals and the control logic illustrated previously, the control unit M40 sends timed earth signals from pins 10 and 1 of connector B which operate the front courtesy lights G10 and the rear ones G25 and G26 .

The courtesy light delay is based on a logic managed by the integrated services control unit located under the dashboard and can be summed up as follows: when any of the four doors is unlocked, all the front and rear courtesy lights are activated with a delay: a period of 6 seconds from the time of unlocking the locks using a key or remote control; a period of 6 seconds from closing one of the doors previously opened; this period is interrupted when the ignition is switched ON (this function makes it possible to enter the vehicle and insert the key in the lock barrel) a period of 3 minutes if one of the doors is left open (this function means that the battery is not run down if the vehicle is left with one of the doors open) When one of the other doors is opened the calculation of the timed period starts again from the beginning. The operation of the courtesy lights takes place coming on and going off gradually (dimmer function) and lasts about 3 seconds. The circuit for the courtesy lights is protected by a special fuse in the junction unit.

Operational description The supply for the front courtesy lights ( G10 ) and rear ones ( G25 and G26) arrives directly from the battery (maxifuse J/B1 of B5 ) via fuse F10 of the junction unit B1 . They are switched on via a direct earth signal (permanently activated) at pin 1 for the courtesy lights or at pin 3 by a signal from the integrated services control unit M40 . The control unit M40 receives a supply directly from the battery - pin 8 of connector B - from the line for maxifuse J/B2 of B5 via shunt fuse B19 and ignition operated (INT) - pin 7 of connector B - from the line for shunt fuse B26 . Pin 13 of connector B provides the earth. The control unit receives door unlocking and opening signals that arrive: at pins 3 and 2 of connector B: opening of one of the front doors N50 and N51 (left and right, respectively); at pins 12 and 18 of connector B: opening of one of the rear doors N55 and N56 (left and right, respectively). On the basis of the above signals and the control logic illustrated previously, the control unit M40 sends timed earthed signals from pins 10 and 1 of connector B which control the front courtesy lights G10 and rear ones G25 and G26 .

Description The horns are operated by pressing one of the two sides of the steering wheel. The horn circuit is protected by a special fuse and controlled by a specific relay located in the junction box. For safety reasons, the horns can be operated at any time, even when the key is turned to OFF (or removed).

Functional description The system for the horns is supplied through the horn relay R2 , located in the junction unit B1 from the direct line from the battery through the fuse F13 - always for B1 - and the maxifuse J/B1 for B5 . The coil for the relay R2 is energized with an earth signal when one of the switches on the steering wheel is closed; on versions with Air Bags, they are connected to the steering column switch unit H5 by the clock spring. The relay R2 thereby supplies the high tone horns P10 and the lone tone horns P11 .

Description The windscreen wash/wipe system is operated by a stalk switch on the right side of the steering wheel. The stalk switch can be set to five positions that correspond to different functions: windscreen wiper off (standstill); intermittent operation; continuous slow operation; continuous medium-fast operation; temporary fast operation (unstable stalk position). The windscreen wiper function is operated by pulling the stalk switch slightly toward the steering wheel. This action operates the washer pump. If the stalk switch is held in position, the windscreen wiper also operates (continuous operation). The windscreen wiper carries on working for a few sweeps after the stalk switch is released. The windscreen wiper and washer can be operated with the ignition key turned to ON. The operation of the windscreen wiper is governed by an electronic device, inside the motor, which produces the intermittent function and controls the operation of the actual windscreen wiper motor. The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse and is operated by the ignition-operated relay located in the junction unit.

Functional description The windscreen wiper stalk of the stalk unit H5 selects the various operating modes of the windscreen wash/wipe. The stalk unit H5 is supplied at pin 3 of connector D from the ignition-operated line (INT/A) of the relay R1 protected by the fuse F14 : both are contained in the junction unit B1 . The supply for the relay R1 comes from the direct line of the maxifuse J/B1 of B5 , whilst the coil is supplied by the line (INT/A) protected by the fuse B26 . Depending on the pre-selected function, the stalk unit H5 (connector A) sends the following control signals to the internal electronic device to the windscreen wiper motor N15: from pin 2 for continuous fast operation: the signal reaches the motor directly; from pins 3, 4 for continuous slow and medium-fast operation: the signal arrives from the intermittent device and is then sent to the motor The windscreen wiper motor N1 5 is then connected to earth. It consists of the actual geared motor, the end of travel contacts and the electronic adjustment and control device. When operated, the windscreen washer switch on the steering column switch unit H5 , sends two signals from pin 8 and pin 9 of connector A, which reach the pump for operating the windscreen washer N22 directly (the operation of this pump N22 in the opposite direction operates the "rearscreen washer" function: ). See E3021 REAR WINDOW WASH/WIPE

Description The rearscreen wiper is operated by turning the ring nut on the end of the lever located on the right of the steering wheel. By pushing the lever gently towards the steering wheel the rearscreen washer function is activated; the same pump is used as for the windscreen washer, but it rotates in the opposite direction and sends the detergent fluid to the rear. If the lever is kept pressed, the rearscreen wiper comes on and operates for a few moments after the lever is released. The rearscreen wash/wipe can only be operated with the ignition switched ON. The rearscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse (which also protects the windscreen wash/wipe circuit) and operated by the ignition-operated relay, located in the junction unit. The rearscreen wiper is regulated by a device inside the actual rearscreen wiper motor.

Functional description The special switch for the steering column switch unit H5 controls the operation of the rearscreen wash/wipe. The stalk unit H5 is supplied at pin 3 of connector D from the ignition-operated line (INT/A) of the relay R1 protected by the fuse F14 : both are contained in the junction unit B1 . Description The rear window heater element, door mirror demister coils and the windscreen heater element absorb a considerable amount of energy. They must therefore be turned off once they have been working for a certain period of time. The engagement of the resistances for defrosting the rearscreen and the external rear view mirrors is controlled, in a timed fashion, by the special button, in the switch unit in the centre of the dashboard; the button, which is dimly lit when the ignition is switched on, comes on brightly when the heated rear windscreen is switched on. The defrosting circuit is protected by a special fuse and controlled by a specific relay located in the junction box.

Functional description The heated rear windscreen relay R3 , located in the junction unit B1 , controls the simultaneous activation of the demisting of both the rear windscreen P55 and the external rear view mirrors P60 and P61 . The relay R3 is supplied by the direct line from the battery through the fuse F11 - always for B1 - and the maxifuse J/B1 for B5 . The coil for the relay R3 is energized by the line controlled by the ignition (INT/A) and is protected by fuse B26 . By pressing the demisting button, an earth signal is sent from the unit H90 which, in addition to giving a command to the coil for R3 , activates the switching on of the LED inside the actual control unit. The electronics inside unit H90 manage the demisting of the rear windscreen, in a timed fashion, removing the earth from the control button. Once energized, the relay R3 controls the rearscreen P55 and protects the mirrors through another protective fuse ( B16 ). The switch control unit H90 has an ignition-operated supply (INT/A) from the line of fuse B27 which lights up the LEDs in the actual switch unit.

Description The two external rear view mirrors are adjusted by a special device next to the front courtesy light which is lit up when the ignition is switched on. The two mirrors are adjusted by a single button pressed in the four directions: a switch selects the right or left mirror. The button, which can be pressed in four directions, controls two electric motors located in each of the two mirrors: one motor rotates the mirror on a horizontal axis, while the other on a vertical axis. The adjustment circuit for the rear view mirrors is protected by the fuse which protects other supplies controlled by the ignition. The mirrors can only be adjusted with the ignition switched ON.

Functional description The two-way switch controlling mirrors H3 0 operates electrical motors located in the right and left electrically-operated door mirrors P60 and P61 respectively. The switch is supplied when the ignition is switched on (INT/A) by the line for fuse B27 at pins 7 and 8 for H30 , whilst pin 5 is earthed. Description The door lock motors are operated simultaneously upon a command: from the key; from the front door switches (knobs); from the remote control (if present) Locking operation: when the key is used on one of the two front doors or the remote control is operated when the doors are firmly shut and the front locks locked, all four side doors are locked simultaneously Unlocking operation: when the key is used on one of the two front doors, with front locks locked, or the remote control is operated, all four doors are unlocked. This control logic is controlled by the specific control unit in the driver's glove compartment The control unit also carries out a series of safety checks: the control unit checks the actual status of the locks: the "lock" or "unlock" command is only executed with the doors properly closed: if the door being operated is not shut properly, the command is inhibited; if the door opposite that being operated is not shut properly, and an immediate "repulsion" is carried out (i.e. the opposite action is carried out to "realign" the locks). if there is a rapid succession of alternating lock/unlock commands, the control unit only carries out the first three commands without activating the inhibition. Similarly if 8/9 opening and closing actions are carried out in 20 seconds (the last is always a closure), the circuit is then inhibited for about 30 s. the circuit can be further inhibited if the battery voltage falls below 9 V within 20 ms. from the start of activation of the lock/unlock actions. During the inhibition time (30 s), the commands are ignored. The locking or unlocking command is also carried out via the remote control receiver, both on versions with an alarm and on versions with a door remote control only. On versions with an alarm, the locking or unlocking command is also carried out via the remote control receiver. The central locking circuit is protected by a special fuse next to the junction unit.

Functional description The M80 central locking control unit controls the operation of the circuit. The M80 control unit (pin +) is supplied directly by the battery via the line protected by the special fuse B19 ; pin (-) provides the reference earth. Control unit M80 receives input signals coming from locks N50 and N51: for locking, if the earth signal goes from pin 2 to pin 3 of M80 ; for unlocking, if the earth signal goes from pin 3 to pin 2 of M80 . The same signals arrive from pins 5 and 6 of the receiver for the remote control M35 . On versions with an alarm, the same signals arrive from pins 5 and 6 of the receiver for the remote control M35 . In accordance with the logic illustrated previously, control unit M80 simultaneously controls the two front locks N50 and N51 and the rear locks N55 and N56 from pins 1M and 2M: locking signal; 12V from pin 2M and earth to pin 1M unlocking signal: 12V from pin 1M and earth to pin 1M

Description The integrated services electronic control unit manages the operation of the boot lock release actuator on the command of: from the inside, through the special button located next to the driver's seat; from the outside, via the key and the rear lock The command is only given if the vehicle is parked (i.e. with a speed signal below 4 km/h). If the doors are locked, the command is possible only from inside and with the key ON. if the doors are released (open), the command can be given from outside or inside.

Functional description The integrated services control unit M40 manages the operation of the circuit. The control unit M40 is supplied directly by the battery - in 8 of connector B - from the line for maxifuse J/B2 of B5 via fuse B19 . Pin 13 of connector B provides the earth. An earth signal is sent to the control unit M40 , at pin 17 of connector B by operating the special control H71 . Description The electric windows in the front doors are operated through the switches in the handles in the front driver's door (both windows) and the front passenger door (passenger side only). The operation is manual: the glass only goes up/down when the button is pressed. Both windows can only be operated when the ignition is on. The control switch symbols are lit when the key is turned to MAR. The circuit for the electric windows is protected by two special fuses, one for the driver's side and one for the passenger side and is controlled by a specific relay (which also operates the rear electric windows); all of these are next to the junction unit.

Functional description The electric windows relay J65 controls the operation of the front electric windows circuit. The electric windows relay is supplied by the direct line from the battery through the maxifuse J/B2 for B5 . The coil for the relay is supplied when the ignition is switched on (INT) from the line for fuse F8 for the junction unit B1 and is always earthed: the relay is therefore always energized when the ignition is switched on (INT). In this way, the line protected by fuses B22 , for the driver's side and B23 for the passenger side, supply the switches H40 (driver's front electric window switch in the front driver's door), H41 (passenger front electric window switch in the passenger side front door) and H50 (electric window switch in passenger side front door) wih the LEDs which light up the actual switches. Operating the switches sends a supply and an earth to the left electric window motor N60 or the right one N61 ; reversing the signals according to the contact which is closed, determines the direction of rotation of the actual motor.

Description The electric windows in the front doors are operated through the switches in the handles in the front driver's door (both windows) and the front passenger door (passenger side only). The electric windows are operated by pressing the appropriate switch: for the driver's window: the operation is manual (the glass goes up/down only when the button is pressed) when the button is held down for 60 to 300 milliseconds; the operation is instead automatic (the glass continues to go up/down to the end of travel, even if the button is released) when the button is held down for over 300 milliseconds; if the button is pressed again during movement of the glass, the glass is stopped instantly; if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, it is ignored (it is considered to have been knocked accidentally). the passenger window can only be operated manually. Both windows can only be operated when the ignition is on. This logic is controlled by the electric windows control unit, in the driver's glove compartment. The control unit also carries out a series of safety checks: the stopping of the electric windows (switching off the electric supply to the motor) is determined when the glass reaches the end of travel at top or bottom, or if an obstacle blocks the glass. This is regulated by checking the motor current. if there are faults on the electrical circuits, the control unit switches the system off temporarily (for example if the motor control signals are interrupted or if the absorbed current is below the usual values); if there is a fault in the control buttons (short circuit, or buttons jammed in the pressed position), the control unit switches the system off temporarily The control switch symbols are lit when the key is turned to MAR. The control circuit for the front electric windows is protected by a specific fuse, next to the junction unit.

Functional description The special front electric windows control unit M81 ensures the correct operation of the circuit. The direct supply from the battery reaches the control unit M81 (pin 30) from the line for the maxifuse J/B2 for B5 protected by fuse B22 , pin 31 provides the reference earth for the control unit. The control unit is then supplied at pin 15 from the line controlled by the ignition (INT) protected by fuse F8 for the junction unit B1 . The switches H40 (left electric window), H41 (right electric window in left front door) and H50 (right electric window in right front door) are supplied directly by the actual control unit, at pin 87 (common supply). There are two further connections, for the left electric window H40 , at pins P9 and P10, which receive the command signals for the left front electric window motor N60 , operated by the control unit by pins M4 and M5. The right front electric window motor N61 is operated directly by the switches H41 and H50 , which provide suitable earth and supply signals to determine the direction of rotation of the motor. All the switches have specific LEDs which light up when they are supplied.

For safety reasons, a special lock switch in the panel next to the switches cuts off the power supply to the rear switches to prevent accidental operation, for example, by children, making it possible to use the switches in the panel only. The rear electrically-operated windows will work only when the key is turned to MAR. The control switch symbols are lit when the key is turned to MAR. The circuit for the electric rear windows is protected by a special fuse and controlled by a special relay (which also controls the front electric windows). Both are next to the junction unit.

Functional description The electric windows relay J65 controls the operation of the front electric windows circuit. The electric windows relay is supplied by the direct line from the battery through the maxifuse J/B2 for B5 . The coil for the relay is supplied when the ignition is switched on (INT) from the line for fuse F8 for the junction unit B1 and is always earthed: the relay is therefore always energized when the ignition is switched on (INT). In this way, the line protected by fuse B17 supplies switches H47 (left), H48 (right) and H55 (rear electric windows lock) whose supply is controlled by the ignition (INT/A) and are connected to earth; in this way they are also lit up when the ignition is switched ON. When these switches are operated - if switch H55 is in the go ahead position - they send the control signals (positive and negative) to the switches in the rear doors H53 and H54 and from there to the motors N65 (left) and N66 (right): reversing the signals according to the contact which has been closed, determines the direction of rotation of the actual motor.

Description The electric windows in the rear doors are operated by means of switches located in each of the rear doors. The operation of the rear windows takes place automatically, in accordance with the following logic which depends how the button is pressed. for opening the windows: the operation is manual (the glass goes up/down only when the button is pressed) when the button is held down for 60 to 300 milliseconds; the operation is instead automatic (the glass continues to go up/down to the end of travel, even if the button is released) when the button is held down for over 300 milliseconds; if the button is pressed again during movement of the glass, the glass is stopped instantly; if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, it is ignored (it is considered to have been knocked accidentally). for closing the windows: the operation is only manual This control logic is controlled by the specific control unit under the dashboard on the passenger side. The control unit also carries out a series of safety checks. The stopping of the electric windows (switching off the electric supply to the motor) is determined when the glass reaches the end of travel at top or bottom, or if an obstacle blocks the glass. This is regulated by checking the motor current. If there are faults on the electrical circuits, the control unit switches the system off temporarily, for example if: the motor control signals are interrupted or if the current uptake is below the usual values. there is a fault in the control buttons (short circuit, or buttons jammed in the pressed position For safety reasons a special lock switch in the dashboard allows the power supply to the rear switches to be excluded to prevent accidental operation, for example, by children. The rear electrically-operated windows will work only when the key is turned to MAR. The control switch symbols are lit when the key is turned to MAR. The control circuit for the rear electric windows is protected by a specific fuse, next to the junction unit.

Functional description The control unit M82 manages the operation of the electric rear windows. The direct supply to the control unit M82 - pins 7 and 2 of connector A - arrives from the direct line from the battery via maxifuse J/B2 of B5 and protected by fuse B17 . The supply controlled by the ignition (INT) reaches pin 2 of connector B, via the line protected by fuse F8 of the junction unit B1 . Pins 9 and 10 of connector A and pin 1 of connector B provide the reference earth. The rear electric windows switch H55 is supplied by the line controlled by the ignition (INT) rotected by fuse F8 of the junction unit B1 : with the button pressed (rear electric windows enablement) the switches in the doors H53 (left) and H54 (right) are also supplied. When the switches are operated, they send command signals (positive and negative) to the rear electric windows control unit M82; the above signals reach: pins 10 and 20 of connector B from the left switch H53 ; pins 9 and 19 of connector B from the right switch H54 ; The control unit M82 controls the electric windows as described above: from pins 3 and 10 of connector A it sends commands to the rear left motor N65 . from pins 1 and 8 of connector A it sends commands to the rear right motor N66 . When the positive and negative signals are reversed, the motor direction of rotation is also reversed.

Description The vehicle is available with two electrically operated sun roofs - front and rear which provide additional ventilation for the passenger compartment and guarantee a rapid exchange of air, when necessary, thereby increasing passenger comfort. The system can be activated by two switches, which can be operated from the front seats, and are located near the courtesy light. The motors operate in the following way: pressing the switch firstly gradually raises the rear of the transparent section until it reaches the spoiler position and then moves the sliding section from this position to the rear end of travel position. The operations are carried out in reverse to close the roof. The control system for each roof is located at the front of it: it consists of a single unit which includes the actual motor and a special electronic control. The electronics of the rear roof also include a special safety function: whilst the roof is closing, the movement is interrupted or reversed if an obstacle is detected by a Hall effect sensor located on the motor. This function makes it possible to stop the closing of the roof is there is an opposing force of more than around 1 kg (e.g. a finger, hand). The sunroof can only be operated with the ignition on. The switches are lit up when the ignition is switched ON. The power circuit is controlled by a relay which also controls the other optional services and is protected by a specific fuse, both of which are located next to the junction unit.

Functional description The optional services relay J60 controls the sun roof power circuit. The coil for the relay J60 is energized when the ignition is switched on (INT) from the line for fuse F8 of the junction unit B1 , whilst the supply to the relay contact arrives directly from the battery via the maxifuse J/B2 line of B5 and is protected by the sun roof fuse B14 . The two switches H61 and H62 receive a supply from the relay J60 (the switches are also lit up thanks to the specific LEDs). Front roof: the operation of the switch H61 in either direction sends the motor N36 a supply or an earth thereby determining the direction of rotation and the consequent movement of the roof. Rear roof: the operation of the switch H62 similarly controls the control unit M83 . The latter is also supplied by a direct line ( J/B1 ) protected by fuse F10 of B1 : according to the commands received by the switch H62 it operates the motor N37 . The lines for pins 9, 11 and 12 connect the control unit to the Hall effect sensor inside the motor.

Description The vehicle is available with two electrically operated sun roofs - front and rear which provide additional ventilation for the passenger compartment and guarantee a rapid exchange of air, when necessary, thereby increasing passenger comfort. The system can be activated by two switches, which can be operated from the front seats, and are located near the courtesy light. The motors operate in the following way: pressing the switch firstly gradually raises the rear of the transparent section until it reaches the spoiler position and then moves the sliding section from this position to the rear end of travel position. The operations are carried out in reverse to close the roof. The control system for each roof is located at the front of it: it consists of a single unit which includes the actual motor and a special electronic control. The electronics of the rear roof also include a special safety function: whilst the roof is closing, the movement is interrupted or reversed if an obstacle is detected by a Hall effect sensor located on the motor. This function makes it possible to stop the closing of the roof is there is an opposing force of more than around 1 kg (e.g. a finger, hand). The sunroof can only be operated with the ignition on. The switches are lit up when the ignition is switched ON. The power circuit is controlled by a relay which also controls the other optional services and is protected by a specific fuse, both of which are located next to the junction unit.

Functional description The optional services relay J60 controls the sun roof power circuit. The coil for the relay J60 is energized when the ignition is switched on (INT) from the line for fuse F8 of the junction unit B1 , whilst the supply to the relay contact arrives directly from the battery via the maxifuse J/B2 line of B5 and is protected by the sun roof fuse B14 . The two switches H61 and H62 receive a supply from the relay J60 (the switches are also lit up thanks to the specific LEDs). Front roof: the operation of the switch H61 in either direction sends the motor N36 a supply or an earth thereby determining the direction of rotation and the consequent movement of the roof. Rear roof: the operation of the switch H62 similarly controls the control unit M83 . The latter is also supplied by a direct line ( J/B1 ) protected by fuse F10 of B1 : according to the commands received by the switch H62 it operates the motor N37 . The lines for pins 9, 11 and 12 connect the control unit to the Hall effect sensor inside the motor.

Description There are three current sockets on the vehicle: one is located in the centre of the dashboard in the ashtray, one is always in the dashboard in front of the passengers and the third is located in the luggage compartment. The front ashtray is lit up when the side lights are on; it houses a standard type current socket; the socket ring nut is also lit up when the side lights are on. The front socket contains the cigar lighter resistance, which can be used for connection to other instruments or equipment (provided they operate on 12 V). To operate the cigar lighter, simply press the knob: after a few seconds it pops out automatically, ready for use. The other two current sockets are exactly the same. The power sockets all have a heat protection device: if devices with high energy absorption are connected, this protection cuts off the supply. The circuit for the current socket/cigar lighter is protected by a specific fuse and is controlled by a relay located in the junction unit. The other current sockets, on the other hand, are protected by a special fuse and are controlled by the optional services relay; both are located next to the junction unit. The sockets are only supplied when the ignition is switched ON. Do not connect equipment more powerful than 180 W (15A absorption).

Functional description The cigar lighter current socket P50 is supplied to pin 2 from the line for relay R1: the line is controlled by the ignition INT/A and protected by fuse F15 : both are located in the junction unit B1 . The supply for the relay R1 comes from the direct line of the maxifuse J/B1 of B5 , whilst the coil is supplied by the line (INT/A) protected by the fuse B26 . Pin 1 for the socket P50 provides the earth. The ring nut for the current socket is lit up (at pin 3) with the side lights on by means of the line coming from the steering column switch unit H5 switch and is protected by the fuse F2 of the junction unit ( ). See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS As far as the other currents sockets P51 and P52 are concerned, they are supplied at pin 2 via the line for the relay J61 . This is supplied by the maxifuse J/B2 line of B5 , whilst the coil is supplied by the line controlled by the ignition (INT/A) protected by the fuse B27 . The supply for the two current sockets is then protected by the specific fuse B15 .

Description A device allows the headlamp beam to be adjusted, directly from the driver's seat, in accordance with the load. The headlamps are thus always aligned quickly and correctly. The adjustment device consists of a motor mounted on each of the two headlamps which tilts them as appropriate, lowering the light beam if the car is heavily laden, and raising it if the load decreases. A specific knob in the dashboard selects the four positions indicated: position 0 - up to three persons in the front seats; position 1 - six persons; position 2 - six persons with luggage in the boot; position 3 - driver and maximum load, all stowed in the boot. The device is only enabled when the dipped headlamps are switched on. The headlamp adjustment circuit is protected by the same fuses as the dipped beam headlamps circuit, located in the junction unit.

Functional description The headlamp alignment device H15 is supplied at pin 2 - with the dipped headlamps on - by a line coming from the steering column switch unit H5 : in involves a supply controlled by the ignition (INT/A) for the line protected by the fuse F5 for the junction unit B1 . The supply is maintained even when the main beam headlamps are switched on, through the special relay J45 ( ). See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS Pin 4 of device H15 is earthed, whilst pin 1 sends the signal to adjust the motors N30 (left) and N31 (right), through a resistance divider which alters the output voltage according to which of the four positions has been selected. Motors N30 and N31 contain a transducer that establishes actual motor travel on the basis of the voltage of an adjustment signal received by pin 2 from device H15 whilst pin 1 is earthed. Motors N30 and N31 are supplied, at pin 3, by the same line for the circuit for the dipped headlamps and the line protected by the fuse F3 for the junction unit B1 ( ). The device therefore only works when the dipped headlamps are switched on. See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS

Description A device allows the headlamp beam to be adjusted, directly from the driver's seat, in accordance with the load. The headlamps are thus always aligned quickly and correctly. The adjustment device consists of a motor mounted on each of the two headlamps which tilts them as appropriate, lowering the light beam if the car is heavily laden, and raising it if the load decreases. A specific knob in the dashboard selects the four positions indicated: position 0 - up to three people in the front seats; position 1 - six persons; position 2 - six persons with luggage in the boot; position 3 - driver and maximum load, all stowed in the boot. The device is only enabled when the dipped headlamps are switched on. The headlamp adjustment circuit is protected by the same fuses as the dipped beam headlamps circuit, located in the junction unit.

Functional description The headlamp alignment device H15 is supplied at pin 2 - with the dipped headlamps on - by a line coming from the steering column switch unit H5 : in involves a supply controlled by the ignition (INT/A) for the line protected by the fuse F5 for the junction unit B1 , via the special relay J45 . See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS Pin 4 of device H15 is earthed, whilst pin 1 sends the signal to adjust the motors N30 (left) and N31 (right), through a resistance divider which alters the output voltage according to which of the four positions has been selected. Motors N30 and N31 contain a transducer that establishes actual motor travel on the basis of the voltage of an adjustment signal received by pin 2 from device H15 whilst pin 1 is earthed. Motors N30 and N31 are supplied, at pin 3, by the same line for the circuit for the dipped headlamps and the line protected by the fuse F5 for the junction unit B1 . See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS The device therefore only works when the dipped headlamps are switched on.

Description The headlight light beam can be adjusted directly from the driver's seat depending on the load. The correct headlamp alignment is quickly achieved in this way. The adjustment device takes the form of a motor fitted on both dipped beams. It is able to tilt the headlamps to lower the light beam if the car is particularly loaded and raise the lamps when the load reduces. A special knob located in the dashboard, to the right of the steering wheel, can be placed in four different positions: position 0 - up to three persons in the front seats; position 1 - six persons; position 2 - six persons plus load in the luggage compartment; position 3 - driver plus maximum permitted load all stowed in the luggage compartment. The device is enabled only with the dipped beams on. The headlamp alignment circuit is protectd by the dipped headlamp circuit fuses located in the junction unit.

Operational description The headlight alignment device H15 receives a supply at pin 2 - with the dipped headlights on - from a line coming from the steering column switch unit H5 : the supply is ignition operated (INT/A) for the line protected by fuse F5 from the junction unit B1 via a special relay J45 Vedere E2011 LUCI ANABBAGLIANTI . Pin 4 of the device H15 is earthed, whilst a signal leaves pin 1 and reaches pin 7 of the headlights F10 (left) and F11 (right, produced by means of a resistive distributor which varies the output tension depending on which of the four positions is selected. The motors located in the headlights F10 (left) and F11 (right) are supplied at pins 3, pins 6 of F10 and F11 by the same line for the dipped headlights circuit, line protected by fuse F5 from the junction unit B1 Vedere E2011 LUCI ANABBAGLIANTI . The device only works with the dipped beams on.

Description This is a device that allows easy manoeuvring whilst parking: when reverse gear is engaged, it signals to the driver that an obstacle, which may be outside of the range of vision, is being approached. It operates according to an ultrasound sonar principle: four ultrasound transducers are located inside the rear bumper. They send signals to a control unit which processes this information determining the distance of possible obstacles. A speaker controlled by the control unit emits an intermittent sound, proportional to the distance of the obstacle detected. The control unit is activated with reverse gear engaged: in these conditions, it energizes the transducers and sends them a signal request, receiving the response signals. The control unit emits a signal with an intermittent sound through the special speaker: the frequency of this sound increases gradually as the bumper approaches an obstacle: when the distance calculated goes below 25 cm, the sound becomes high-pitched and constant. If the distance of the obstacle detected increases, or if the driver disengages reverse gear, the sound stops. If the distance of the obstacle detected remains constant, the sound stops after about 3 seconds. For more details and information on the operation of the system, Characteristic of working principle 5580H DISPOSITIVO RILEVAMENTO OSTACOLI IN PARCHEGGIO . The control unit is located inside the luggage compartment, on the right hand side; there is a buzzer next to the contorl unit. The system receives a power supply from the reversing lights circuit ( Vedere E2022 LUCI RETROMARCIA )

Operational description Engaging reverse gear closes the switch I20 and provides a power supply to the right rear light cluster F31 Vedere E2022 LUCI RETROMARCIA . The same line, from connector B of F31, supplies the parking sensor control unit M84 at pin 1 of connector and provides an earth at pin 16 of the same connector The parking sensor speaker P44 sends two signals to the parking sensor control unit M84 from pins 2 and 10 of connector A; pins 9 and 6 of the same connector are bridged. The connectors for the four parking sensors K97 are all connected to connector B of the control unit M84, respectively: to pins 9, 5, 12 of M84 to the sensor K97A ; to pins 7, 3, 10 of M84 to the senor K97B ; to pins 1, 2, 6 of M84 to the sensor K97C ; to pins 8, 4, 1 of M84 to the sensor K97D ;

Description The vehicle is prepared for the installation of a radio system. This preparation comprises: radio compartment radio supply cables front speakers located in the doors, and separate tweeters, located in the front pillars; rear speakers, located in the doors; leads connecting the radio to the speakers; aerial; aerial coaxial cable. The radio circuit is supplied with the key turned to the ON position, or directly from the battery (which allows tuning settings, security codes, etc. to be stored). The above two lines are protected by two fuses in the junction unit. In addition to the radio there is also a supply with the side lights on to light up the radio controls. A radio, specially designed for this vehicle, is available on request and is fitted during production. Full radio specifications and operating instructions are given in the OWNER'S HANDBOOK. On request, the radio can be connected to a CD player, located under the outside front passenger seat.

Description Preparation for the "TELEPASS " © is available (for the Italian market only). This communcations system pays motorway tolls without the need to stop at a paybooth. An electronic device fitted to the car emits a sound pulse that is picked up by a receiver on the paybooth, through which the car drives at moderate speed but without stopping. The predisposition takes the form of a specific rear view mirror that contains housing for this electronic device in addition to device wiring. The device is operated when the ignition key is turned to ON. The above line is protected by a fuse which also supplies other services.
Functional description The connector for the "TELEPASS" D76 consists of a supply controlled by the ignition (INT/A) (pin 3) from the line protected by fuse B27 and a connection (pin 1) to earth C30 .
