Description The right button in the climate control control panel in the centre of the dashboard switches on the air cooling and dehumidifying circuit, activating the air conditioning compressor. The above button enables the operation of the air cooling circuit; but the actual switching on of the compressor also depends on the intervention of: the 4 stage pressure switch, located in the refrigerant circuit, which stops the air conditioning being switched on if the pressure of the fluid is too low or too high; the engine control unit which, according to the engine management logic, excludes the operation of the compressor, for example in the case of high engine temperatures or in the case of high engine loads (sharp acceleration). For further details see Characteristic of working principle 5040 AIR CONDITIONING CASING AND COMPONENTS The compressor supply circuit is controlled by a specific relay, located in the engine compartment in the fuse and relay box; the relay supply line is protected by a specific fuse in the fuse box.

Functional description The relay J20 controls the compressor engagement circuit. The relay is supplied by relay R1 : line controlled by the ignition INT/A, protected by fuse F15 : both are housed in the junction unit B1 . The supply for the relay R1 comes from the direct line of the maxifuse J/B1 of B5 , whilst the coil is supplied by the line (INT/A) protected by the fuse B26 : this line also supplies the switch unit H80 ,. via fuse B27 . The relay J20 coil is supplied by the line protected by fuse B36 and the main relay J10 . See E5030 PETROL ENGINE ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT Press the appropriate button on unit H80 to sends a signal to 4-stage pressure switch K1.: This, in turn, if the pressure in the circuit is correct, does not interrupt the signal which reaches the engine control unit M10 (pin 48 of connector A). Control unit M10 uses its own internal software to send a signal (from pin 41of connector A) to activate the compressor which energizes the relay J20 . The relay operates the solenoid valve, at 12 V, which switches on the air conditioning compressor L20 . The second signal energizes the relay J34 coil which activates the first speed for the fan N85 , according to the description . See E6020 AIR CONDITIONING The fan operates at the first speed if the button for engaging the compressor is pressed, even if the control knob H81 is in position '0'.

Characteristic of working principle 5040 AIR CONDITIONING CASING AND COMPONENTS The above mentioned control unit enables the operation of the air cooling circuit; but the actual switching on of the compressor also depends on the intervention of: the 3 stage pressure switch, located in the refrigerant circuit, which stops the air conditioning being switched on if the pressure of the fluid is too low or too high; the engine control unit which, according to the engine management logic, excludes the operation of the compressor, for example in the case of high engine temperatures or in the case of high engine loads (sharp acceleration). The cooling circuit is also controlled by engaging the 'MAX DEF' rapid demisting function (last position of the distribution knob) Characteristic of working principle 5040 AIR CONDITIONING CASING AND COMPONENTS The compressor supply circuit is controlled by a specific relay, located in the engine compartment, in the relay and fuse box; the relay supply line is protected by a specific fuse in the fuse box.

Functional description The relay J20 controls the compressor engagement circuit. The relay is supplied by relay R1 : line controlled by the ignition INT/A, protected by fuse F15 : both are housed in the junction unit B1 . The supply for the relay R1 comes from the direct line of the maxifuse J/B1 of B5 , whilst the coil is supplied by the line (INT/A) protected by the fuse B26 : this line also supplies the switch unit H80 ,. via fuse B27 . The relay J20 coil is supplied by the line protected by fuse B36 and the main relay J10 . Control unit M10 uses its own internal software to send a signal (from pin 41of connector A) to activate the compressor which energizes the relay J20 . Description The right button in the climate control control panel in the centre of the dashboard switches on the air cooling and dehumidifying circuit, activating the air conditioning compressor, according to the complex control logic managed by the climate control system control unit. Characteristic of working principle 5040 AIR CONDITIONING CASING AND COMPONENTS The above mentioned control unit enables the operation of the air cooling circuit; but the actual switching on of the compressor also depends on the intervention of: the 3 stage pressure switch, located in the refrigerant circuit, which stops the air conditioning being switched on if the pressure of the fluid is too low or too high; the engine control unit which, according to the engine management logic, excludes the operation of the compressor, for example in the case of high engine temperatures or in the case of high engine loads (sharp acceleration). The cooling circuit is also controlled by engaging the 'MAX DEF' rapid demisting function (last position of the distribution knob) Characteristic of working principle 5040 AIR CONDITIONING CASING AND COMPONENTS The compressor supply circuit is controlled by a specific relay, located in the engine compartment, in the relay and fuse box; the relay supply line is protected by a specific fuse in the fuse box.

Functional description The relay J20 controls the compressor engagment circuit. The relay is supplied by relay R1 : line controlled by the ignition INT/A, protected by fuse F15 : both are housed in the junction unit B1 . The supply for the relay R1 comes from the direct line of the maxifuse J/B1 of B5, whilst the coil is supplied by the ignition-operated line (INT/A): this line also supplies switch unit H81 via fuse B27 The relay J20 coil is supplied by the line protected by fuse B36 and the main relay J10 . See E5030 PETROL ENGINE ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT Pressing the button in group H80 , sends a signal to the climate control system control unit M70 - pin B5 - ; this checks the conditions for engaging the compressor and sends another signal to the 4 stage pressure switch K10 at pin A13. This, in turn, if the pressure in the circuit is correct, does not interrupt the signal which reaches the engine control unit M10 (pin 48 of connector A). According to its internal control software, the control unit M10 sends (from pin 14 of connector A) a command to engage the compressor which energizes the relay J20. The relay operates the solenoid valve, at 12 V, which switches on the air conditioning compressor L20 . The engagement of the compressor is also controlled, in the same way as described above, by the switch I65 for the 'MAX DEF' rapid demisting function.

Description To increase protection against theft attempts, an electronic immobilizer system known as the "FIAT CODE-2" system has been adopted. The keys are fitted with an electronic Transponder device, which send a coded signal to a special CODE electronic control unit. If it recognizes the code sent, it allows the engine to be started up. The code used in the communication, which takes place via aerial, changes each time the car is started up (rolling code). The code cannot therefore be reproduced, even with electronic scanners. The main function of the Code control unit is to identify the code in the ignition key. The control unit contains a secret code which is used to communicate with the key Transponder. The control unit contains all enabled key codes in its memory, together with the code used in the communication between Code control unit and engine management unit. When the key is turned to MAR for for the first time, if the key is identified correctly, the code is transferred to the engine management unit and is then indelibly linked to the Code control unit. For more details . see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 5580E anti-theft device The Code system has supply lines for the control unit protected by the maxifuse which also protects the engine management system, by a specific fuse and by the fuse which protects other supplies controlled by the ignition: the two fuses are located in the engine compartment in the relay and fuse box.

Functional description The CODE control unit M20 is supplied at pin 3 by the battery from the line for the maxifuse EFI (UGD) of B5 and is protected by fuse B35 . The supply controlled by the ignition (15/54) reaches pin 8 through the line protected bu fuse B25 . Pin 4 is earthed. The line leading from pin 6 is a serial line leading to engine management unit M10 , which is responsible for identifying the key and exchanging codes. It is possible to "read" the control unit autodiagnostic system, by connecting to the autodiagnostic connector R10 from pin 5 of the control unit M20 . The autodiagnostic system also produces the signal for the "CODE failure" warning light, located in the instrument panel E50 : it involves an earth signal coming out of pin 2 of the control unit M20 . The instrument panel E50 is controlled by the ignition (INT) at pin 2 of connector A from the line protected by fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 : when an earth signal reaches pin 12 of connector C, the "CODE warning" light comes on. A second control unit connector is connected via two leads to the aerial, fitted coaxially to the ignition key, in order to detect key insertion and rotation.

Description The alarm system offers volumetric and perimeter protection. In effect, an electronic control unit checks: the status of doors, boot and bonnet via switches in the locks (perimeter control) the presence of a moving object inside the passenger compartment, via volumetric sensors (volumetric control) the condition of the system supply cables (both directly from the battery and those controlled by the ignition) the condition of emergency key supply leads the operation of ignition switch The control unit is equipped with a self-test function which detects and memorizes faults in the control unit itself and the system components and also checks the condition of the connecting cables. The control unit also memorizes the number of times the alarm is activated and set off. The control unit operating software may be altered to meet regulations governing the use of alarm systems applicable in different markets. The electronic control unit, which also incorporates the siren, is located at the front, under the wheel arch to the left of the engine compartment. The receiver is an electronic device which receives the transmitter signal. It is located in a concealed position under the dashboard. It is connected to the control unit via the serial line and directly manages the following system functions: it receives, decodes and manages the remote control signals it locks and unlocks the doors it stores the codes of enabled sending units. The receiver also has its own autodiagnostic function which detects and memorizes faults in the actual receiver and the components connected to it and it checks the condition of the connecting cables. The emergency key for deactivating the system is located on the left of the dashboard, next to the junction unit. It cuts out the system, for example in the case of repair interventions. The same switches as for the central locking system are used to control the doors and lids. A special switch is also located on the bonnet catch. The volumetric sensors check for car intruders. They are located near the front courtesy light. The deterrent LED is in the centre of the dashboard and signals the status of the system (on, off, etc.) and any possible irregularities. The deterrent LED is in the control panel in the centre of the dashboard, in place of one of the switches, and signals the status of the system (on, off, etc.) and any possible irregularities. For more details . see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 5580E anti-theft device The alarm system control unit has direct supply lines and lines controlled by the ignition protected by two fuses in the junction unit., such as the remote control unit receiver. The alarm system control unit and the remote control receiver has direct supply lines and lines controlled by the ignition, protected by three fuses located in the junction unit.

Functional description The alarm system is controlled by alarm control unit M30 integral with the siren. The control unit is supplied directly by the battery at pin 3 of connector A from the line for the maxifuse J/B1 of B5 and is protected by fuse F10 of the junction unit B1 and at pin 7 of connector B (supply for the direction indicators) from the line protected by fuse F9 ; still for the junction unit B1 . The supply controlled by the ignition (INT) reaches pin 12 of connector B for control unit M30 . through the line protected by fuse F1 of the control unit B1 . Pin 9 of connector A is earthed. The control unit M30 controls the closure of the doors via switches N50 , N55 , N51 , N56 which send an earth signal, if the door is open, to pins 8, 15, 9, 16 of connector B. The bonnet lid is controlled by switch I10 , which is connected to pin 18 of connector B, while the boot lid is controlled by switch I11 , which is connected to pin 1 of connector B (the same switch turns on the boot light: ) See E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT Pin 13 of connector B supplies the emergency switch H70 which sends the ON and OFF signals to pins 7 and 4, respectively of connector A. Pin 1 of connector A of M30 sends the control signal for the alarm LED, located - up to May '99 - in the switch control panel H90 , pin 11 of connector A or located separately in the centre of the dashboard E40 . Volumetric sensor unit K62 receives supply and earth signals from pins 8 and 11 of connector A of M30 , and sends on the alarm control signal to pin 12 of connector A of M30 . Pins 1 and 2 of connector B of M30 produce control signals for turn signals ( ). See E2020 DIRECTION INDICATORS / HAZARD WARNING LIGHTS The receiver for the remote control M35 is supplied directly by the battery at pin 3 from the line protected by fuse F10 and by a line protected by the ignition (INT) at pin 7 from the line protected by fuse F1 ; both fuses are located in the junction unit B1 . Pin 4 is earthed. M35 (pins 5 and 6) gives out signals for "door locking" and "door unlocking", respectively, for the central locking control unit M80 ( ). See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING The control unit M30 and the receiver M35 are both equipped with an autodiagnostic system which can be used by connecting to connector R10 : it receives signals from pin 6 of connector A of M30 and from pin 2 of the remote control receiver M35 . This serial line also acts as a connection between M30 and M35 .

Description The alarm system offers volumetric and perimeter protection. In effect, an electronic control unit checks: the status of doors, boot and bonnet via switches in the locks (perimeter control) the presence of a moving object inside the passenger compartment, via volumetric sensors (volumetric control) the condition of the system supply cables (both directly from the battery and those controlled by the ignition) the condition of emergency key supply leads the operation of ignition switch The control unit is equipped with a self-test function which detects and memorizes faults in the control unit itself and the system components and also checks the condition of the connecting cables. The control unit also memorizes the number of times the alarm is activated and set off. The control unit operating software may be altered to meet regulations governing the use of alarm systems applicable in different markets. The electronic control unit, which also incorporates the siren, is located at the front, under the wheel arch to the left of the engine compartment. The receiver is an electronic device which receives the transmitter signal. It is located in a concealed position under the dashboard. It is connected to the control unit via the serial line and directly manages the following system functions: it receives, decodes and manages the remote control signals it locks and unlocks the doors it stores the codes of enabled sending units. The receiver also has its own autodiagnostic function which detects and memorizes faults in the actual receiver and the components connected to it and it checks the condition of the connecting cables. The emergency key for deactivating the system is located on the left of the dashboard, next to the junction unit. It cuts out the system, for example in the case of repair interventions. The same switches as for the central locking system are used to control the doors and lids. A special switch is also located on the bonnet catch. The volumetric sensors check for car intruders. They are located near the front courtesy light. The deterrent LED is in the centre of the dashboard and signals the status of the system (on, off, etc.) and any possible irregularities. For more details . see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 5580E anti-theft device The alarm system control unit has direct supply lines and lines controlled by the ignition protected by two fuses in the junction unit., such as the remote control unit receiver. The alarm system control unit and the remote control receiver has direct supply lines and lines controlled by the ignition, protected by three fuses located in the junction unit.

Description The alarm system offers volume-sensing and perimeter protection against intrusion into the vehicle. An electronic control unit controls: the state of the doors and lids, via switches in the catches (perimeter control) the presence of a moving object inside the passenger compartment, by means of volumetric sensors. (volumetric control) the condition of the system supply leads (both direct from the battery and ignition-operated) the operation of the ignition switch. The control unit is equipped with an autodiagnostic function that detects and memorizes faults and problems with the actual control unit and the system components and checks the condition of the connecting cables. The control unit also memorizes the number of times the alarm has been activated and set off. The control unit operating software may be altered to meet regulations governing the use of alarm systems applicable in different markets. The electronic control unit, which also incorporates the siren, is located at the front, under the engine compartment right wheel arch. The receiver is an electronic device which receives the transmitter signal. It is concealed uner the dashboard. A special switch is located on the bonnet lock. The control unit also produces a "doors open" signal, which is activated if even only one of the doors is not properly shut and is sent to the instrument panel. Vedere E4010 STRUMENTO DI BORDO . The volumetric sensors check that there are no intrustions in the vehicle. They are located near the front courtesy light The deterrent LED is located in the centre of the dashboard and signals the system status (on, off, etc.) plus any faults. For more details see Characteristic of working principle 5580E DISPOSITIVO ANTIFURTO . Description The electronic anti-lock brake system (BOSCH 5.3 ABS) governs braking pressure sent to the wheels and prevents loss of grip under all tyre and road surface conditions. The system is designed to complement the normal mechanical braking system and not to replace it. In this way it ensures effective safety in the case of anomalies: the ABS uses the same fluid as the conventional mechanical braking system. Four sensors fitted to the four wheels inform the electronic control unit of wheel speed at every moment. In this way, they detect wheel lock, wheel slip and loss of grip. Under these conditions, the control unit sends specific instructions to solenoids that modulate hydraulic circuit pressure to eliminate lock and restore the car to within grip limits. This ensures the shortest possible stopping distance, without losing control of the steering. Two adjustment solenoids (one for pressure charging, the other for pressure discharging) are fitted for each wheel. The sensors are active, i.e. they consist of a Hall-effect receiver that faces a magnetic coding device built into the hub bearing. Under these conditions, the signal is less influenced by electromagnetic interference and temperature. The control unit also controls brakeforce distribution over the rear axle and thus replaces the mechanical lload proportioning valve used previously (EBD function: Electronic Brake Distribution). The control unit is equipped with a self-diagnostic function: when an error occurs in the ABS system, a warning light is turned on and the system is simultaneously deactivated. Under these conditions, the car brakes using only the conventional system. When the control unit detects an error in the EBD function, it simultaneously turns on the "insufficient brake fluid level" and "handbrake on" warning light as well as the ABS warning light. Under these conditions, the rear brake distribution control is also deactivated and the car must be driven with great care. For more details see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 3340 A(B.S. ANTI-LOCK BRAKING SYSTEM .) The supply lines for the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by a special maxifuse, located near the control unit, and by a fuse in the engine compartment in the relay and fuse box.

Functional description ABS electronic control unit M50 is supplied (at pin 17 and 18) directly by the battery via a line protected by ABS maxifuse B7 . The supply controlled by the ignition (15/54) reaches pin 15 from the line protected by the specific fuse B31 . The control unit is earthed via pins 19 and 16. The four sensors K70 , K71 , K75 , K76 send wheel speed signals to pins 6-7, 4-5, 8-9 and 1-2, respectively of M50 . The brake pedal switch I30 sends a go ahead signal to pin 14 of the control unit M50 : in effect, the operation of the ABS is excluded unless the brake pedal is pressed; this signal arrives from the line controlled by the ignition (INT) protected by fuse F1 of the junction unit (it is the same signal which switches on the lights - ) See E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS If the control unit M50 detects problems relating to the ABS function, it sends the instrument panel E50 a signal, from pin 20, which lights up the "ABS failure" warning light. the "ABS failure" warning light is a so-called "intelligent" light: thanks to a special operating circuit inside the instrument, it not only comes on to signal a fault in the ABS system, but also if there is no connection or a short circuit to earth in the circuit which connects the instrument with the control unit If the problems involve the EBD function, the control unit also sends a signal from pin 21 to the "insufficient brake fluid level and handbrake" warning light which comes on together with the "ABS failure" warning light. This is an earth signal and makes the warning light come on because the instrument panel E50 supply is controlled by the ignition (INT) from the line protected by fuse F1 of the junction unit B1 . The autodiagnostic data can be read by connecting to connector R10 : it receives signals from pin 11 of the control unit M50 via the special diagnostic line.

Description The electronic anti-lock brake system (BOSCH 5.3 ABS) governs braking pressure sent to the wheels and prevents loss of grip under all tyre and road surface conditions. The system is designed to complement the normal mechanical braking system and not to replace it. In this way it ensures effective safety in the case of anomalies: the ABS uses the same fluid as the conventional mechanical braking system. Four sensors fitted to the four wheels inform the electronic control unit of wheel speed at every moment. In this way, they detect wheel lock, wheel slip and loss of grip. Under these conditions, the control unit sends specific instructions to solenoids that modulate hydraulic circuit pressure to eliminate lock and restore the car to within grip limits. This ensures the shortest possible stopping distance, without losing control of the steering. Two adjustment solenoids (one for pressure charging, the other for pressure discharging) are fitted for each wheel. The sensors are active, i.e. they consist of a Hall-effect receiver that faces a magnetic coding device built into the hub bearing. Under these conditions, the signal is less influenced by electromagnetic interference and temperature. The control unit also controls brake force distribution over the rear axle and thus replaces the mechanical load proportioning valve used previously (EBD function: Electronic Brake Distribution). The control unit is equipped with a self-diagnostic function: when an error occurs in the ABS system, a warning light is turned on and the system is simultaneously deactivated. Under these conditions, the car brakes using only the conventional system. When the control unit detects an error in the EBD function, it simultaneously turns on the 'insufficient brake fluid level' and 'handbrake on' warning light as well as the ABS warning light. Under these conditions, the rear brake distribution control is also deactivated and the car must be driven with great care. For more details see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 3340 A(B.S. ANTI-LOCK BRAKING SYSTEM .) The supply lines for the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by a special maxifuse, located near the control unit, and by a fuse in the engine compartment in the relay and fuse box.

Description The electronic anti-lock brake system (BOSCH 5.7 ABS with ASR) governs braking pressure sent to the wheels and prevents loss of grip under all tyre and road surface conditions. This is combined with an ESP (Electronic Stability Program) system, which controls vehicle stability by modulating drive torque and braking the wheels differentially, if there is a loss of grip, thus helping to return the car to its correct trajectory. The ESP system acts on the engine and brakes to generate a stabilising torque when the ABS sensors detect conditions that could lead to the vehicle slipping. The ESP system includes the following specific components over and above those of the ABS: a sensor which detects the steering wheel position (steering sensor); a sensor which detects the vehicle's rotation around the vertical axis and side acceleration (centrifugal force) (yaw sensor); a sensor that detects pressure on the hydraulic ABS unit (pressure sensor) The ESP system is always connected to the ASR system. The ASR system increases vehicle stability and active safety by controlling drive wheel slip. If slip is caused by excessive power transmission, it cuts in to reduce engine power through communication with the engine management control unit. if slip is detected at a single wheel, the system cuts in to brake the slipping wheel by acting on the modulation solenoid. ASR comes on automatically whenever the engine is started. The system can be deactivated by operating a button in the dashboard. When the system is off, an LED on the button comes on at the same time as a warning light on the control panel. The ESP, on the other hand, switches on automatically each time the engine is started up and cannot be switched off. ASR/ESP warning light: the warning light flashes when the system cuts in to notifiy the driver that the ASR system has cut in due to road surface grip conditions. When th econtrol unit detects an error in the ASR function or the ESP function, it lights up the warning light constantly. As far as the ABS function is concerned, . See E7020 ABS For more details, Characteristic of working principle 3340 A(B.S. ANTI-LOCK BRAKING SYSTEM .) The supply lines for the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by a special maxifuse, located near the control unit, and by a fuse in the engine compartment in the relay and fuse box. The ASR off button is protected by a special shunt fuse, located next to the junction unit.

Functional description The ABS electronic control unit M50 is supplied (at pins 2 and 6) directly by the battery via a line protected by ABS maxifuse B7. The supply controlled by the ignition (15/54) reaches pin 23 from the line protected by the specific fuse B31. The control unit is earthed via pins 1 and 5. The brake pedal switch I30 with the N.A. contact sends an enablement signal to pin 32 of control unit M50; this signal arrives from the line controlled by the ignition (INT) protected by fuse F1 of the junction unit (it involves the same signal that lights up the brake lights . Steering sensor K58 is supplied by ABS control unit M50 at pin 39 and receives a reference earth from pin 21: the signal that detects sudden changes in steering direction is sent via the CAN line to engine management control unit M1 and to the ABS control unit M50, pins 24 and 40. Yaw sensor K74 is supplied from ABS control unit M50 at pin 39, while it receives a reference earth from pin 21: control and command signals are exchanged with ABS control unit M50 , at pins 8, 9, 10 and 41. Pressure sensor K72 is supplied from ABS control unit M50 at pin 42, while it receives a reference earth from pin 25: the pressure detection signal is sent to pin 26 of ABS control unit M50 . The ABS control unit M50 is connected, via the special CAN line, from pin 22, to the instrument panel E50 to manage the ABS failure warning light, the EBD warning light and the ASR/ESP warning light. The ASR OFF button, located in the switch unit H90, connector C, sends a deactivation signal to pin 27 of M50, whilst the signal that switches on the LED when the system is switched off is sent from pin 18; ; switch H90C is supplied by the line controlled by the ignition (INT) protected by shunt fuse B10. Description The car may be fitted with an electronically-controlled safety system that sets off the front seat belt pretensioners and the driver's air bag, passenger air bag and sidebags in the case of frontal and/or side impact of a certain severity. In the case of a side impact of a certain magnitude, the corresponding side Air Bag and Window Bags are activated (only on the side where the impact has taken place). An electronic control unit manages the entire system by controlling all the components and activating the restraint systems (pretensioners and airbags) as necessary. The control unit is located under the centre console and is rigidly fixed to the bodyshell: in this way the deceleration sensors located inside it are close to the centre of gravity and detect deceleration for the entire vehicle accurately. There is an accelerometric sensor on the two front door pillars which, in the case of a side impact, transmits a signal to the control unit. This signal is also processed inside the control unit which, as a result, decides on the operation of the Side Bag and Window Bag on the side where the impact has taken place. The driver's Air Bag module is located in the centre of the steering wheel; A clock spring device allows the airbag module connection leads to turn with the steering wheel without the risk of breakage. The two front Air Bag modules have two stage operation: the first stage is for slight impacts and the second stage for more severe impacts. The two stages have two separate charges which inflate the bag to 60% (first stage) and 40% (second stage). The two passenger Air Bag modules (two gas generators which inflate a large single bag) are located in the dashboard, fixed directly to the vehicle crossmember by a special bracket. The passenger Air Bag can be manually deactivated via a special switch - which can be operated by a key - located above the dashboard in the driver's glove compartment. With the key in the OFF position, the control unit also controls the operation of the special 'passenger Air Bag disabled' warning light. The Side Bag is housed in the outer part of the exterior front seats. The window bags take the form of a curtain which inflates and positions itself between the occupant's head and the side windows. The folded bag is located under the roof panel, whilst the rear pillar houses the gas generator. The front seat pretensioners are devices built into the front seat belt reel. The belt fitted to the central front seat is equipped with a mechanical pretensioner: see . Characteristic of working principle 7065 SEAT BELTS AND ACCESSORIES The control unit is self-diagnostic. it detects and memorizes any faults it recognizes the various components and the type of fault it signals the onset of these faults via the special warning light. System activations following a particularly serious impact are memorized by the control unit. For more details . Characteristic of working principle 5580C air bag system The supply line for the system control unit is protected by a special fuse next to the junction unit. When operations are carried out to the Air Bag system the recommended safety instructions must be followed precisely. For more details Characteristic of working principle 5580C air bag system

Functional description The control unit for the Air Bag system M60 is controlled by the ignition (INT) at pin 12 from the line protected by shunt fuse B32. Pin 1 of connector A is connected to the special earth C50, as are pins 17 and 32 of connector B. The side impact detection sensors K66 (driver's side) and K67 (passenger side) send signals to pins 24-26 and 25-27 respectively of connector B of the control unit M60. When a frontal impact of a certain severity (depending on the control strategy, data from the above two sensors and sensors incorporated in the control unit) is detected, the control unit sends control signals to operate the front modules: to driver's Air Bag Q9, via the steering wheel clockspring D47 (from pins 23-24 of connector A of M60) in the case of first stage activation; to driver's Air Bag Q9, via the steering wheel clockspring D47 (from pins 19-20 of connector A of M60) in the case of second stage activation; to the outer passenger Air Bag Q12 and the inner bag Q13 (from pins 21-22 and 17-18 of connector A of M60); to the driver's pretensioner Q20 (from pins 1-2 of connector B of M60) and the passenger pretensioner Q21 (from pins 3-4 of connector B of M60). A signal from passenger Air Bag disabling switch H75 reaches pin 11 of connector A of M60, supplied from pin 10 of connector A of M60. When side impact of a certain severity (dependent on the software setting) is detected, the control unit sends control signals to set off the modules: to driver's side bag Q30 (from pins 5-6 of connector B of M60); to passenger side bag Q31 (from pins 9-10 connector B of M60); to driver's rear side bag Q43 (from pins 13 and 14 of connector B of M60); to passenger side rear air bag to the driver's window bag Q40 (from pins 7-8 of connector B of M60); to the passenger window bag Q41 (from pins 11-12 of connector B of M60). When the system self-diagnostic function detects a fault or an impact is detected, control unit M60 sends a signal -from pin 8 of connector A - to the Air Bag fault warning light located in instrument panel E50 - pin 27 of connector A. the 'Air Bag fault' warning light is a so-called 'intelligent' warning light: thanks to a special operating circuit inside the instrument, it comes on, not only to signal a fault in the Air Bag system, but also if there is no connection or a short circuit to earth in the circuit which connects the instrument with the control unit. When the passenger Air Bag is disabled, the control unit M60 sends a signal, from pin 7 of connector A, to the 'passenger Air Bag deactivation' warning light, located in the instrument panel E50 - pin 28 of connector A. These signals are earthed and turn on the warning lights since instrument E50 is ignition-activated (INT/A) - pin 19 of connector A - from a line protected by fuse F1 of junction unit B1. Self-diagnostic data can be read by connecting the unit to connector R10: it receives signals from pin 6 of connector A of the control unit M60 through the relevant tester line.

Description The car is fitted with an electronically-controlled safety system which, in the case of a front-end crash of some severity, activates the driver's and passenger Air Bags. The electronic control unit manages the entire system, checking all the components and when necessary activating the Air Bags. The control unit is situated on the floor in a central position under the dashboard, and is secured rigidly to the bodywork; in this way the deceleration sensors located inside it are near the baricentre and can detect precisely the deceleration of the entire car. The driver's Air Bag module is located in the centre of the steering wheel; it is fitted on a tilting plate which enables the horn to be operated. The plate houses a metal container which holds the folded airbag and a gas generator that inflates the bag. A clockspring cable allows the Air Bag module connecting cables to follow the rotation of the steering wheel without the risk of breaking. The two passenger Air Bag modules (two gas generators which inflate a large single bag) are located in the dashboard, fixed directly to the vehicle crossmember by a special bracket. The passenger Air Bag can be manually deactivated via a special switch - which can be operated by a key - located above the dashboard in the driver's glove compartment. When the key is turned to OFF, the control unit also controls the activation of a passenger air bag disablement warning light on the instrument panel. The control unit comes with a self-diagnostic function. it detects and memorizes any faults it recognizes the various components and the type of fault it signals the onset of these faults via the special warning light. System activations following a particularly serious impact are memorized by the control unit. For more details . Characteristic of working principle 5580C air bag system The system control unit supply line is protected by a special fuse located next to the junction unit. there are two possible configurations for the system. - the 'standard' configuration. includes the driver's Air Bag and two pretensioners. The complete configuration also includes a passenger Air Bag and disabling device. carefully observe the safety regulations when working on the airbag system. For more details Characteristic of working principle 5580C air bag system

Functional description The control unit for the Air Bag system M60 is controlled by the ignition (INT) at pin 15 from the line protected by fuse B32 . Pin 24 is connected to the specific earth C50 , like pin 30, on the 'complete' versions, i.e. those with a passenger Air Bag. (on versions with a driver's Air Bag only, pin 30 is not connected). When an impact of a set severity (determined by the control software) is detected, the control unit sends control signals to set off the modules: to driver's Air Bag Q9 , via the steering wheel clockspring Q10 (from pins 1 and 2): to the outer passenger Air Bag Q12 and the inner one Q13 (from pins 13 and 14 and 3 and 4, respectively); Pins 5 and 8 are connected to the passenger Air Bag disabling switch H75 . When the system self-diagnostic function detects a fault or an impact is detected, control unit M60 sends a signal -from pin 13 - to the Air Bag fault warning light located in instrument panel E50 . the 'Air Bag fault' warning light is a so-called 'intelligent' warning light: thanks to a special operating circuit inside the instrument, it comes on, not only to signal a fault in the Air Bag system, but also if there is no connection or a short circuit to earth in the circuit which connects the instrument with the control unit. When the passenger Air Bag is disabled, the control unit M60 sends a signal, from pin 20, to the 'passenger Air Bag deactivation' warning light, located in the instrument panel E50 . Description The car is fitted with an electronically-controlled safety system which, in the case of a front-end crash of some severity, activates the driver's and passenger Air Bags. In the case of a side impact of a certain magnitude, the corresponding side Air Bag is activated (only on the side where the impact has taken place). The electronic control unit manages the entire system, checking all the components and when necessary activating the Air Bags. The control unit is situated on the floor in a central position under the dashboard, and is secured rigidly to the bodywork; in this way the deceleration sensors located inside it are near the baricentre and can detect precisely the deceleration of the entire car. There is an accelerometric sensor at the base of the two front door pillars which, in the case of a side impact, transmits a signal to the control unit. The driver's Air Bag module is located in the centre of the steering wheel; it is fitted on a rocker plate which allows the operation of the horns. The plate houses a metal container which holds the folded airbag and a gas generator that inflates the bag. A clockspring cable allows the Air Bag module connecting cables to follow the rotation of the steering wheel without the risk of breaking. The two passenger Air Bag modules (two gas generators which inflate a large single bag) are located in the dashboard, fixed directly to the vehicle crossmember by a special bracket. The passenger Air Bag can be manually deactivated via a special switch - which can be operated by a key - located above the dashboard in the driver's glove compartment. When the key is turned to OFF, the control unit also controls the activation of a passenger air bag disablement warning light on the instrument panel. The Side Bag is housed in the outer part of the front seat and is activated in the case of a side impact detected by the sensor. The control unit comes with a self-diagnostic function. it detects and memorizes any faults it recognizes the various components and the type of fault it signals the presence of faults via a warning light. System activations following a particularly serious impact are memorized by the control unit. For further details see . see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 5580C air bag system The supply line for the system control unit is protected by a special fuse next to the junction unit. there are two possible configurations for the system. - the "basic" configuration with a driver's Air Bag, side bags and two pretensioners. - the full configuration which also includes a passenger Air Bag and disabling device. carefully observe the safety regulations when working on the Air Bag system. For further details see " see DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION: 5580C air bag system

Functional description The control unit for the Air Bag system M60 is controlled by the ignition (INT) at pin 15 from the line protected by fuse B32 .
